chunks: And with this chain, from Al-Ridha (peace be upon him), from his father Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: As-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said:

Indeed, a man may be between himself and Paradise have a distance greater than that from the earth to the Throne, due to the abundance of his sins. But it is not so except that he weeps from the fear of Allah, the Exalted, repenting for them, until the distance between him and Paradise becomes closer than the distance between his eyelid and his eyeball.
ai.seo_question: How does sincere repentance affect the distance between a sinner and Paradise?
ai.summary: Imam As-Sadiq (peace be upon him) illustrates the transformative power of *tawbah* (repentance) by contrasting the immense spiritual distance caused by accumulated sins with the immediate proximity achieved through tearful remorse. This narration, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq, emphasizes that divine mercy can bridge the gap between the earth and the Throne, turning a sinner into a near neighbor of Paradise through the sincerity of their weeping. It highlights the Shia emphasis on the efficacy of emotional repentance (*bukaa*) as a means of expiating major sins and restoring spiritual closeness to God.
